clue.text: Incorporeal presence returning in "Hamlet" is bewitched

indicators.note: returning says the hidden letters are read backwards
in says the letters sit inside the quoted words that follow it

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A ghostly presence haunts a production of Hamlet, casting a spell over the play.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' marks the run hamLET IS BEWitched; 'returning' turns ETISBEW round.
explanation.definitionFit: A site on the internet gives a person or firm a presence that has no physical body, hence incorporeal.

clue.text: Opportunity for survivor to adopt name

indicators.note: to adopt means to take something in, so the survivor's word takes in the name's letter

parts.note: a widow is the surviving spouse

explanation.surface: A chance for a bereaved person to take on a new name.
explanation.definitionFit: A window, as in a window of opportunity, is a brief chance to act.

clue.text: Unusually large type of car

definitions.meaning: a ... harvest or crop is an exceptionally big one
the small dodgem driven at fairgrounds

explanation.definitionFit: Bumper as an adjective means abundant or huge; bumper cars are fairground dodgems.

clue.text: Nice detail rendered coarse

indicators.note: rendered means made into something else, so these letters are converted into a new order

explanation.surface: A fine piece of decoration has been made to look crude.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rendered' rearranges the ten letters of NICE DETAIL.
explanation.definitionFit: Indelicate and coarse are synonyms describing vulgar or tasteless behaviour.

clue.text: Monster drops one, going back to German city

indicators.note: going back says the remaining letters are read in reverse order
drops means loses, so a letter is removed from the monster's name

parts.note: Nessie is the Loch Ness Monster
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A monster sheds a member and heads back to a city in Germany.
explanation.walkthrough: 'drops' takes I out of NESSIE, leaving NESSE; 'going back' turns that round.
explanation.definitionFit: Essen is an industrial city in the Ruhr region of western Germany.

clue.text: Posh jerks welcoming qualified person's advance

parts.note: U means upper-class, as in U and non-U usage

indicators.note: welcoming means receiving inside, so the exercises' letters take in the graduate

parts.note: physical jerks are exercises, done in PE lessons
a grad, short for graduate, is someone who has qualified

explanation.surface: Snobbish idiots greet a professional's career move.
explanation.walkthrough: 'jerks' looks like an insult; it is physical jerks, PE. The setter has called his own website upgrade the inspiration.
explanation.definitionFit: An upgrade is a step up or improvement, an advance in level or quality.

clue.text: Reveal a Frenchwoman suppressing passion?

indicators.note: suppressing means holding down or keeping in, so the woman's word holds the passion inside it

parts.note: un is French for a, and she is a woman
heat means passion or strong feeling

explanation.surface: Expose a French lady who is holding back her ardour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Frenchwoman' splits in two: the French for 'a', and a woman; the passion goes inside the woman, after her first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: To unsheathe a blade is to draw it out of its cover, so to reveal or bare it.

clue.text: Belted little girl, reportedly

indicators.note: reportedly means as people say it, so the word is heard rather than read

parts.note: Gert is a pet form of the girl's name Gertrude

explanation.surface: A small girl who has been hit, as rumour has it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Belted' looks like hit; it means wearing a belt.
explanation.definitionFit: Girt is an old past tense of gird, meaning encircled with a belt or girdle.

clue.text: Haply confused about horse's relief work of sorts

indicators.note: about means around, so the jumbled letters go around the horse
confused means mixed up, so these letters are jumbled

parts.note: a nag is a horse, usually an old one

explanation.surface: A rider is muddled about the horse in some sculpted relief.
explanation.walkthrough: 'confused' rearranges the letters of 'Haply' into ALYPH, and 'about' wraps that round the horse after its first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: An anaglyph is an ornament carved in low relief, or a stereoscopic picture, so a kind of relief work.

clue.text: Fire up motor with second pole reversed, carrying monarch

indicators.note: carrying means holding within, so the altered motor holds the monarch
reversing a pole swaps north for south, so the second north letter becomes a south letter

parts.note: an engine is a motor
ER is the royal cipher, Elizabeth Regina

explanation.surface: Start an engine after swapping its second terminal and with the king on board.
explanation.walkthrough: Of a motor's two N letters (north poles), the second turns into S, a south pole, making ENGISE; 'carrying' puts the monarch inside.
explanation.definitionFit: To energise is to give energy to, to fire up or invigorate.

clue.text: Retiring academic interrupted by Scholar-Gipsy, perhaps

indicators.note: interrupted by means broken into, so the scholar's degree goes inside
retiring means drawing back, so the academic's word is read backwards

parts.note: a don is a university teacher
an MA, a Master of Arts, is a scholar

explanation.surface: A withdrawing academic is cut short by Arnold's poem The Scholar-Gipsy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Retiring' turns the academic into NOD. The Scholar-Gipsy is a poem by Matthew Arnold about an Oxford scholar who wanders off to join travellers.
explanation.definitionFit: A gipsy is one example of a traveller who moves from place to place without a fixed home.

clue.text: Whisper about American substitute conceding own goal

indicators.note: about here means turned around, so the American abbreviation is read backwards
conceding means giving up, so the substitute loses some letters

parts.note: a surrogate is a substitute
OG is the football abbreviation for own goal

explanation.surface: Muttering about an American replacement player who gave away an own goal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' turns US into SU; 'conceding' takes OG from SURROGATE, leaving SURRATE.
explanation.definitionFit: To susurrate is to whisper or murmur softly, a rustling sound.

clue.text: Australian herdsman's vernal refreshment in European river

indicators.note: in means placed inside, so the rearranged letters go into the river

parts.note: the Oder is a river on the German-Polish border

indicators.note: refreshment means making new, so these letters are given a fresh order

explanation.surface: An outback stockman enjoys a spring revival on a continental river.
explanation.walkthrough: 'refreshment' turns 'vernal' into VERLAN, which 'in' places inside the river.
explanation.definitionFit: In Australia an overlander is a drover who moves livestock over long distances.

clue.text: Commentary on 1 across left in toilet

indicators.note: in means placed inside, so the abbreviation goes into the toilet

parts.note: bog is British slang for a toilet

explanation.surface: A remark about an internet page that was left in the lavatory.
explanation.definitionFit: A blog is a running online journal of comment hosted on a site on the internet.

clue.text: Grandiose accommodation for 9 not waterproof on the outside

indicators.note: on the outside says the leaky word wraps round the shelter

parts.note: porous means letting water through
the wanderer at 9 across lives in a tent

explanation.surface: Lodging for a traveller is pretentious but lets the rain in.
explanation.walkthrough: 'accommodation for 9' points to the answer at 9 across, a wanderer, whose home is a TENT.
explanation.definitionFit: Portentous can mean pompous or self-important, which is grandiose in manner.

clue.text: Resort to beginning of psalm: "Closer to Thee", perhaps?

indicators.note: perhaps hints that the hymn line can be rearranged into another form
beginning of means the first letter of the following word

explanation.surface: Turning to the opening of a hymn, Nearer to Thee-style, for consolation.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters of CLOSER TO THEE plus P (beginning of psalm) are the answer plus TO: the first 'to' is subtracted. CLEETHORPES is a seaside resort in Lincolnshire, England.
explanation.definitionFit: Cleethorpes is a seaside town on the Lincolnshire coast of England, a holiday destination.

clue.text: Beg to admit church is bound

indicators.note: to admit means to let in, so the plea takes the church inside

parts.note: entreat means beg

explanation.surface: Ask the church to let you in, since you are obliged to.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bound' looks like obliged; it is a leap, a noun.
explanation.definitionFit: An entrechat is a ballet leap in which the dancer crosses the feet in the air, so a kind of bound.

clue.text: Correctly installing high-volume alarm

indicators.note: installing means putting inside, so the adverb holds the loud marking

parts.note: aright means correctly
ff, fortissimo, is the musical marking for very loud

explanation.surface: Putting in a properly loud burglar alarm.
explanation.walkthrough: 'alarm' looks like a noun; it is the verb, to frighten.
explanation.definitionFit: To affright, an archaic verb, is to frighten or alarm someone.

clue.text: Archivist's instrument

definitions.meaning: a wind instrument played in schools, a kind of flute

explanation.definitionFit: A recorder is both one who keeps records and an end-blown woodwind instrument.

clue.text: Press in the fast lane?

parts.note: fleet means fast
a lane is a street

explanation.surface: Journalism in the overtaking lane.
explanation.walkthrough: Fleet Street in London was the home of the British national newspapers.
explanation.definitionFit: Fleet Street is a metonym for the British national newspapers, the press.

clue.text: Try hard to produce melody

explanation.definitionFit: To strain is to exert oneself; a strain is also a passage of music.

clue.text: Consumer zone sounding like Biblical charity gig?

indicators.note: sounding like says the words are heard rather than spelled

parts.note: an Ark Aid concert would be Noah's version of Band Aid, a fundraising gig

explanation.surface: A shopping area that brings to mind a Bible-themed benefit concert.
explanation.walkthrough: Band Aid and Live Aid were famous charity concerts; Noah's Ark makes it Biblical.
explanation.definitionFit: A shopping arcade is a covered walk lined with shops, a zone for consumers.

clue.text: Villain beheaded bird

indicators.note: beheaded means losing the head, so the first letter goes

parts.note: a crook is a villain

explanation.surface: A criminal executed a bird.
explanation.definitionFit: A rook is a crow-like bird that nests in colonies.

clue.text: Serially eponymous character — one usurping 1,000 in Montmartre, chaotically …

indicators.note: chaotically means in disorder, so the letters are scrambled
usurping means seizing the place of, so one letter takes over another's position

parts.note: M is the Roman numeral for 1,000
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A character in a film series, someone ousting a thousand in Paris's artists' quarter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'usurping' swaps an M of MONTMARTRE for I; 'chaotically' rearranges the result.
explanation.definitionFit: The Terminator is the cyborg title character of a whole series of films named after him.

clue.text: Something sung to man or woman

indicators.note: to means attached to, so the song is added after the man's letter

parts.note: M is the abbreviation for male
an aria is a solo song in an opera

explanation.surface: A song addressed to a man or a woman.
explanation.definitionFit: Maria is a woman's given name.

clue.text: Elevated whip-round for pancake

indicators.note: elevated means lifted up, which in a down clue reads the word upwards

parts.note: the cat, short for cat-o'-nine-tails, is a whip
O is round in shape

explanation.surface: A raised collection for a breakfast pancake.
explanation.walkthrough: 'whip-round' looks like a collection; it is whip (CAT) and round (O).
explanation.definitionFit: A taco is a folded Mexican tortilla, a thin flat bread loosely called a pancake.

clue.text: … animal tender almost taking Defender of the Faith for another

indicators.note: taking means taking in, so the shortened herdsman holds the title
almost means nearly whole, so the last letter is dropped

parts.note: a goatherd tends goats
DF stands for Defender of the Faith, a title of British monarchs

explanation.surface: A livestock keeper almost takes on the monarch's title instead.
explanation.walkthrough: Continues from 22: 'another' means another title character of a film series. 'almost' drops the herdsman's last letter, making GOATHER.
explanation.definitionFit: The Godfather is another title character who gives a series of films its name.

clue.text: Politician at 0o?

parts.note: the figure zero looks like the letter O
the small raised o stands for the degree sign, and BA and MA are both degrees

explanation.surface: A statesman at zero degrees.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue intends 0° (zero degrees); this copy prints the degree sign as a small o. Zero gives O, degrees give BA plus MA.
explanation.definitionFit: Barack Obama is an American politician, elected US president shortly before this puzzle appeared.

clue.text: Vessel received by solicitor in attendance

indicators.note: received by means taken in by, so the vessel goes inside the solicitor

parts.note: a tout solicits business or custom
an urn is a vessel

explanation.surface: A ship is welcomed by a lawyer who is present.
explanation.walkthrough: 'solicitor' looks like a lawyer; it is one who solicits, a tout.
explanation.definitionFit: Turnout is the number of people attending an event.

clue.text: Space capsule initially filling poet's vacancy

indicators.note: filling means going inside, so the space and letter go into the poet

parts.note: Dannie Abse was a Welsh poet
an en is a printer's space

indicators.note: initially means the first letter of the word

explanation.surface: A spacecraft's start fills a writer's empty slot.
explanation.walkthrough: Dannie Abse was a twentieth-century Welsh poet and doctor; the printer's space and capsule's first letter sit after his S.
explanation.definitionFit: Absence and vacancy both mean the state of being empty or not present.
